content.json:
# Detection Engineering Dashboard
Health, coverage, fidelity, efficiency and lifecycle of your Microsoft Sentinel detection portfolio. Built for the Microsoft Defender portal (unified SecOps). Select your **workspaces**, a **time range** and **severity**, then use the tabs to navigate. All log panels query across every selected workspace.

parameters.name: Workspaces
parameters.label: Workspaces (log data)
parameters.description: One or more Log Analytics / Microsoft Sentinel workspaces. Every log panel queries across all selected workspaces and unions the results.

content.json:
## Detection Engineering Overview
Portfolio health at a glance: detection output, rule execution health, and SOC outcomes across the selected time range. Use the tabs above to drill into coverage, rule health, fidelity, incident metrics, ingestion and engineering velocity.

content.query:
let alerts = SecurityAlert | where AlertSeverity in ({Severity});
let incidents = SecurityIncident | where Severity in ({Severity}) | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by IncidentNumber;
let rh = SentinelHealth | where SentinelResourceType =~ "Analytics rule" | where OperationName in~ ("Scheduled analytics rule run", "NRT analytics rule run");
union isfuzzy=true
 (incidents | summarize Value = todouble(count()) | extend Metric = "Incidents", o = 1),
 (incidents | where Status == "Closed" and Classification == "FalsePositive" | summarize Value = todouble(count()) | extend Metric = "False-positive incidents", o = 2),
 (alerts | summarize Value = todouble(count()) | extend Metric = "Alerts fired", o = 3),
 (alerts | summarize Value = todouble(dcount(AlertName)) | extend Metric = "Active detections", o = 4),
 (rh | where Status == "Failure" | summarize Value = todouble(dcount(SentinelResourceName)) | extend Metric = "Rules failing", o = 5),
 (rh | summarize Value = todouble(dcount(SentinelResourceName)) | extend Metric = "Rules executing", o = 6)
| project Metric, Value, o
| sort by o asc
| project Metric, Value
content.title: Key indicators

content.query:
SecurityIncident
| where Severity in ({Severity})
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by IncidentNumber
| where CreatedTime between ({TimeRange:start} .. {TimeRange:end})
| summarize Incidents = count() by bin(CreatedTime, 1d), Severity
| order by CreatedTime asc
content.title: Incidents per day by severity

content.query:
SecurityAlert
| where AlertSeverity in ({Severity})
| summarize Alerts = count() by bin(TimeGenerated, 1d), AlertSeverity
| order by TimeGenerated asc
content.title: Alerts per day by severity

content.query:
SentinelHealth
| where SentinelResourceType =~ "Analytics rule"
| where OperationName in~ ("Scheduled analytics rule run", "NRT analytics rule run")
| summarize Runs = count(),
            Failures = countif(Status == "Failure"),
            Rules = dcount(SentinelResourceName)
| extend ['Failure rate %'] = iff(Runs == 0, 0.0, round(100.0 * Failures / Runs, 1))
| extend Health = case(['Failure rate %'] >= 20, "Unhealthy",
                       ['Failure rate %'] >= 5, "Degraded",
                       "Healthy")
| project Health, Rules, Runs, Failures, ['Failure rate %']
content.title: Analytics rule execution health (range)

content.json:
## Detection Coverage (MITRE ATT&CK)
Coverage derived from **firing** detections in the selected range. Tactics/techniques come from the `SecurityAlert` mappings, and **technique IDs are resolved to their MITRE names** (sub-techniques inherit their parent's name). Alerts with **no MITRE mapping** (shown as *Unknown*) are excluded from the tactic/technique views and surfaced separately in the **Unmapped detections** panel below - that's a detection-hygiene backlog, not real coverage. Pair the gap list with the *designed* coverage on the portal **MITRE ATT&CK** page (rules that exist but haven't fired).

content.query:
SecurityAlert
| where AlertSeverity in ({Severity})
| where isnotempty(Tactics)
| extend TacticsArr = iff(Tactics startswith "[", todynamic(Tactics), split(Tactics, ","))
| mv-expand T = TacticsArr to typeof(string)
| extend Tactic = trim(" ", tostring(T))
| where isnotempty(Tactic) and Tactic !~ "Unknown"
| summarize Alerts = count() by Tactic
| order by Alerts desc
content.title: Alerts by MITRE tactic (mapped only)

content.query:
let allTactics = datatable(Tactic:string, Key:string)
[
 "Reconnaissance","reconnaissance",
 "Resource Development","resourcedevelopment",
 "Initial Access","initialaccess",
 "Execution","execution",
 "Persistence","persistence",
 "Privilege Escalation","privilegeescalation",
 "Defense Evasion","defenseevasion",
 "Credential Access","credentialaccess",
 "Discovery","discovery",
 "Lateral Movement","lateralmovement",
 "Collection","collection",
 "Command and Control","commandandcontrol",
 "Exfiltration","exfiltration",
 "Impact","impact"
];
let firing = SecurityAlert
 | where AlertSeverity in ({Severity})
 | where isnotempty(Tactics)
 | extend TacticsArr = iff(Tactics startswith "[", todynamic(Tactics), split(Tactics, ","))
 | mv-expand T = TacticsArr to typeof(string)
 | extend Key = tolower(replace_string(trim(" ", tostring(T)), " ", ""))
 | where isnotempty(Key)
 | summarize Alerts = count(), Detections = dcount(AlertName) by Key;
allTactics
| join kind=leftouter firing on Key
| extend Alerts = coalesce(Alerts, 0), Detections = coalesce(Detections, 0)
| extend Status = iff(Alerts == 0, "GAP - no firing detection", "Covered")
| project Tactic, Status, Alerts, Detections
| order by Alerts asc, Tactic asc
content.title: Tactic coverage status (all 14 MITRE tactics, gaps first)

content.query:
SecurityAlert
| where AlertSeverity in ({Severity})
| extend NoTactic = isempty(Tactics) or Tactics has "Unknown"
| extend NoTechnique = isempty(Techniques) or Techniques has "Unknown"
| where NoTactic or NoTechnique
| summarize Alerts = count(),
            ['Missing tactic'] = countif(NoTactic),
            ['Missing technique'] = countif(NoTechnique),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
  by Detection = AlertName, Severity = AlertSeverity, Product = ProductName
| order by Alerts desc
| take 100
content.title: Unmapped detections - no MITRE tactic/technique (hygiene backlog)

content.query:

| where isnotempty(AlertName)
| summarize Alerts = count(), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by Detection = AlertName, Severity = AlertSeverity, Tactics, Techniques
| order by Alerts desc
| take 200
content.title: Detection to tactic / technique mapping

content.json:
## Defender & Custom Detections (Advanced Hunting native)
Built on the **`AlertInfo`** advanced-hunting table, so it works natively in the Microsoft Defender portal and spans Defender for Endpoint / Office 365 / Identity / Cloud Apps **and your custom detections** (plus onboarded Sentinel alerts). `DetectionSource has "Custom"` isolates custom-detection rules - the Defender equivalent of analytics-rule authoring. Use this tab when running in Defender XDR or when `SentinelHealth`/`SentinelAudit` logging isn't enabled.

content.query:
AlertInfo
| where Severity in~ ({Severity})
| summarize
    ['Defender alerts'] = todouble(count()),
    ['Custom-detection alerts'] = todouble(countif(DetectionSource has "Custom")),
    ['Custom detections (distinct)'] = todouble(dcountif(Title, DetectionSource has "Custom")),
    ['Detection sources'] = todouble(dcount(DetectionSource)),
    ['Service sources'] = todouble(dcount(ServiceSource))
| project packed = pack_all()
| mv-expand kind=array packed
| project Metric = tostring(packed[0]), Value = todouble(packed[1])
content.title: Defender detection indicators

content.query:
AlertInfo
| where Severity in~ ({Severity})
| summarize Alerts = count() by DetectionSource
| order by Alerts desc
content.title: Alerts by detection source (custom vs Microsoft)

content.query:
AlertInfo
| where Severity in~ ({Severity})
| summarize Alerts = count() by ServiceSource
| order by Alerts desc
content.title: Alerts by service source

content.query:
AlertInfo
| where Severity in~ ({Severity})
| where DetectionSource has "Custom"
| extend SevRank = case(Severity =~ "High", 4, Severity =~ "Medium", 3, Severity =~ "Low", 2, Severity =~ "Informational", 1, 0)
| summarize Alerts = count(), TopRank = max(SevRank), LastSeen = max(Timestamp) by Detection = Title, ServiceSource
| extend ['Highest severity'] = case(TopRank == 4, "High", TopRank == 3, "Medium", TopRank == 2, "Low", TopRank == 1, "Informational", "Unknown")
| project Detection, ServiceSource, Alerts, ['Highest severity'], LastSeen
| order by Alerts desc
| take 100
content.title: Custom detections - volume & severity

content.json:
## Rule Inventory & Health
Sourced from `SentinelHealth` analytics-rule run events (the source of truth for rule execution). `ExtendedProperties.AlertsGeneratedAmount` lets us find **silent** rules (executing but never firing) and **failing** rules without any join. Prioritise fixing high failure-rate rules and reviewing silent rules for broken logic or dead log sources.

> **Interactive:** click any rule in *Per-rule execution health* to load its run history in the detail panel below (click the same row again or clear the selection to reset).

> **This tab needs Sentinel *health* diagnostics.** If panels are empty, enable Microsoft Sentinel **Settings > Settings > Auditing and health monitoring** (streams `SentinelHealth`). Until then, use the **Defender & Custom Detections** tab for live detection signal. This tab covers Sentinel analytics rules; Defender custom detections are on the Defender tab.

content.query:
let rh = SentinelHealth
 | where SentinelResourceType =~ "Analytics rule"
 | where OperationName in~ ("Scheduled analytics rule run", "NRT analytics rule run")
 | extend AlertsGenerated = tolong(ExtendedProperties.AlertsGeneratedAmount);
union isfuzzy=true
 (rh | summarize Value = todouble(dcount(SentinelResourceName)) | extend Metric = "Rules executing", o = 1),
 (rh | where Status == "Failure" | summarize Value = todouble(dcount(SentinelResourceName)) | extend Metric = "Rules with failures", o = 2),
 (rh | summarize gen = sum(AlertsGenerated) by SentinelResourceName | where gen == 0 | summarize Value = todouble(count()) | extend Metric = "Silent rules (0 alerts)", o = 3),
 (rh | summarize runs = count(), fails = countif(Status == "Failure") | extend Value = iff(runs == 0, 0.0, round(100.0 * fails / runs, 1)) | extend Metric = "Run failure rate %", o = 4)
| project Metric, Value, o
| sort by o asc
| project Metric, Value
content.title: Rule portfolio indicators

content.query:
SentinelHealth
| where SentinelResourceType =~ "Analytics rule"
| where OperationName in~ ("Scheduled analytics rule run", "NRT analytics rule run")
| extend AlertsGenerated = tolong(ExtendedProperties.AlertsGeneratedAmount)
| summarize Runs = count(),
            Failures = countif(Status == "Failure"),
            AlertsGenerated = sum(AlertsGenerated),
            (LastRun, LastStatus) = arg_max(TimeGenerated, Status)
  by Rule = SentinelResourceName
| extend ['Failure rate %'] = round(100.0 * Failures / Runs, 1)
| order by ['Failure rate %'] desc, Failures desc
content.title: Per-rule execution health (click a row to drill down)

content.query:
SentinelHealth
| where SentinelResourceType =~ "Analytics rule"
| where OperationName in~ ("Scheduled analytics rule run", "NRT analytics rule run")
| where "{selectedRule}" == "" or SentinelResourceName == "{selectedRule}"
| extend ep = ExtendedProperties
| project TimeGenerated, Rule = SentinelResourceName, Status, Reason,
          Results = tolong(ep.QueryResultAmount),
          AlertsGenerated = tolong(ep.AlertsGeneratedAmount),
          Description
| order by TimeGenerated desc
| take 200
content.title: Run history - selected rule (all rules until one is clicked above)

content.query:
SentinelHealth
| where SentinelResourceType =~ "Analytics rule"
| where OperationName in~ ("Scheduled analytics rule run", "NRT analytics rule run")
| extend AlertsGenerated = tolong(ExtendedProperties.AlertsGeneratedAmount)
| summarize Runs = count(), AlertsGenerated = sum(AlertsGenerated), LastRun = max(TimeGenerated) by Rule = SentinelResourceName
| where AlertsGenerated == 0
| project Rule, Runs, AlertsGenerated, LastRun
| order by Runs desc
content.title: Silent rules (executing, zero alerts)

content.query:
SentinelHealth
| where SentinelResourceType =~ "Analytics rule"
| where OperationName in~ ("Scheduled analytics rule run", "NRT analytics rule run")
| where Status == "Failure"
| project TimeGenerated, Rule = SentinelResourceName, Reason, Description
| order by TimeGenerated desc
| take 200
content.title: Recent failed rule runs (detail)

content.query:
SentinelHealth
| where SentinelResourceType =~ "Analytics rule"
| where OperationName in~ ("Scheduled analytics rule run", "NRT analytics rule run")
| where Status == "Failure"
| summarize Failures = count() by bin(TimeGenerated, 1d)
| order by TimeGenerated asc

content.json:
## Detection Efficacy & Fidelity
Signal-to-noise and analyst outcomes. Noisiest detections are ranked by raw alert volume; fidelity uses closed-incident **classification** (`TruePositive` / `FalsePositive` / `BenignPositive`). Detections that are high-volume and 100% false positive are your top tuning candidates.

content.query:
SecurityAlert
| where AlertSeverity in ({Severity})
| summarize Alerts = count(), Days = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1d)), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
  by Detection = AlertName, Severity = AlertSeverity
| extend ['Alerts per active day'] = round(Alerts * 1.0 / Days, 1)
| order by Alerts desc
| take 50
content.title: Noisiest detections (top 50 by volume)

content.query:
SecurityIncident
| where Severity in ({Severity})
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by IncidentNumber
| where Status == "Closed"
| summarize Total = count(),
            FalsePositive = countif(Classification == "FalsePositive"),
            TruePositive = countif(Classification == "TruePositive"),
            BenignPositive = countif(Classification == "BenignPositive"),
            Undetermined = countif(isempty(Classification) or Classification == "Undetermined")
  by Detection = Title
| extend ['False positive %'] = iff(Total == 0, 0.0, round(100.0 * FalsePositive / Total, 1))
| order by ['False positive %'] desc, Total desc
| take 50
content.title: Detection fidelity by classification

content.query:
SecurityIncident
| where Severity in ({Severity})
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by IncidentNumber
| where Status == "Closed"
| summarize FalsePositive = countif(Classification == "FalsePositive"),
            TruePositive = countif(Classification == "TruePositive")
  by Detection = Title
| top 15 by FalsePositive + TruePositive
| project Detection, FalsePositive, TruePositive
content.title: True vs false positive by detection (top 15)

content.query:
SecurityIncident
| where Severity in ({Severity})
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by IncidentNumber
| where Status == "Closed"
| summarize Total = count(), FP = countif(Classification == "FalsePositive") by Detection = Title
| where Total >= 5 and FP == Total
| project Detection, Incidents = Total, ['All false positive'] = FP
| order by Incidents desc
content.title: Tuning candidates (high volume, all false positive)

content.json:
## Incident Metrics (SOC feedback loop)
How detections translate into analyst work. MTTA/MTTR are medians derived from `SecurityIncident` timestamps (triage ~ first-modified minus created; resolve ~ closed minus created). Watch aging open incidents and unassigned load.

content.query:
let inc = SecurityIncident | where Severity in ({Severity}) | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by IncidentNumber;
union isfuzzy=true
 (inc | extend tta = datetime_diff('minute', FirstModifiedTime, CreatedTime) | where isnotnull(tta) and tta >= 0 | summarize Value = todouble(round(percentile(tta, 50), 0)) | extend Metric = "MTTA median (min)", o = 1),
 (inc | where Status == "Closed" | extend ttr = datetime_diff('hour', ClosedTime, CreatedTime) | where isnotnull(ttr) and ttr >= 0 | summarize Value = todouble(round(percentile(ttr, 50), 1)) | extend Metric = "MTTR median (hrs)", o = 2),
 (inc | where Status != "Closed" | summarize Value = todouble(count()) | extend Metric = "Open incidents", o = 3),
 (inc | summarize Value = iff(count() == 0, 0.0, round(100.0 * countif(Status == "Closed") / count(), 1)) | extend Metric = "% closed", o = 4)
| project Metric, Value, o
| sort by o asc
| project Metric, Value
content.title: Response indicators
Incidents created vs closed per day

content.query:
SecurityIncident
| where Severity in ({Severity})
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by IncidentNumber
| where Status == "Closed"
| summarize Count = count() by Classification = iff(isempty(Classification), "Undetermined", Classification)
content.title: Closed-incident classification

content.query:
SecurityIncident
| where Severity in ({Severity})
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by IncidentNumber
| extend OwnerName = tostring(Owner.assignedTo)
| extend OwnerName = iff(isempty(OwnerName), "Unassigned", OwnerName)
| summarize Incidents = count() by OwnerName
| order by Incidents desc
| take 15
content.title: Incident load by owner (top 15)

content.query:
SecurityIncident
| where Severity in ({Severity})
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by IncidentNumber
| where Status != "Closed"
| extend ['Age (days)'] = round(datetime_diff('hour', now(), CreatedTime) / 24.0, 1)
| project IncidentNumber, Title, Severity, Status,
          Owner = tostring(Owner.assignedTo), ['Age (days)'], CreatedTime
| order by ['Age (days)'] desc
| take 100
content.title: Aging open incidents

content.json:
## Data & Ingestion (detection fuel & cost)
Detections are only as good as their data. Track ingestion volume per table, spot cost drivers, and catch **stale tables** (log sources that stopped ingesting) - a silent killer of detection coverage. Values in GB from the `Usage` table.

content.query:
union isfuzzy=true
 (Usage | summarize Value = round(sum(Quantity) / 1024.0, 1) | extend Metric = "Total GB (range)", o = 1),
 (Usage | where IsBillable == true | summarize Value = round(sum(Quantity) / 1024.0, 1) | extend Metric = "Billable GB (range)", o = 2),
 (Usage | summarize Value = todouble(dcount(DataType)) | extend Metric = "Active tables", o = 3)
| project Metric, Value, o
| sort by o asc
| project Metric, Value
content.title: Ingestion indicators

content.query:
Usage
| where IsBillable == true
| summarize GB = sum(Quantity) / 1024.0 by bin(TimeGenerated, 1d), DataType
| order by TimeGenerated asc
content.title: Billable ingestion (GB/day) by table

content.query:
Usage
| summarize GB = round(sum(Quantity) / 1024.0, 2),
            ['Billable GB'] = round(sumif(Quantity, IsBillable == true) / 1024.0, 2)
  by DataType
| order by GB desc
| take 30
content.title: Top tables by volume

content.query:
Usage
| summarize LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), GB = round(sum(Quantity) / 1024.0, 2) by DataType
| extend ['Days since data'] = round(datetime_diff('hour', now(), LastSeen) / 24.0, 1)
| where ['Days since data'] >= 3
| project DataType, LastSeen, ['Days since data'], GB
| order by ['Days since data'] desc
content.title: Stale tables (no data in 3+ days)

content.json:
## Lifecycle & Deprecations (detection-continuity risk)
Deprecations silently break detections when an ingestion path stops. The most urgent item for a detection-engineering team right now is the **Azure Monitor HTTP Data Collector API**, whose support **ends 14 September 2026** - any custom pipeline still POSTing to it must move to the **DCR-based Logs Ingestion API** (the legacy API also doesn't support Private Link).

> **Which `_CL` tables are actually *Classic*?** That flag isn't in `Usage` or the log rows - it's table *metadata* (`schema.tableSubType` = `Classic` vs `DataCollectionRuleBased`). The **Classic vs DCR-based custom tables** panel below reads it directly from the Log Analytics **Tables** API (Azure Resource Manager), so it gives you the authoritative answer. Rows showing **`Classic`** are the ones tied to the legacy ingestion path - migrate those first.

content.query:
let items = datatable(Milestone:string, Deadline:datetime, Action:string, o:long)
[
 "HTTP Data Collector API - support ends", datetime(2026-09-14), "Migrate to the DCR-based Logs Ingestion API", 1,
 "Log Analytics agent (MMA/OMS) - cloud upload can stop", datetime(2026-03-02), "Migrate remaining agents to Azure Monitor Agent (AMA)", 2,
 "Microsoft Sentinel in the Azure portal - retires", datetime(2027-03-31), "Operate Sentinel in the Microsoft Defender portal", 3
];
items
| extend ['Days remaining'] = datetime_diff('day', Deadline, now())
| extend Status = case(['Days remaining'] < 0, "PASSED",
                       ['Days remaining'] <= 30, "IMMINENT",
                       ['Days remaining'] <= 120, "SOON", "Planned")
| order by o asc
| project Milestone, Deadline, ['Days remaining'], Status, Action
content.title: Deprecation timeline (live countdown)

parameters.name: MetadataWorkspace
parameters.label: Audit workspace
parameters.description: The single workspace whose custom-table metadata (Classic vs DCR) is read via ARM below. Defaults to your first workspace; the ARM Tables API targets one workspace at a time, so switch this to audit each in turn.

content.query: {"version": "ARMEndpoint/1.0", "data": null, "headers": [], "method": "GET", "path": "{MetadataWorkspace}/tables", "urlParams": [{"key": "api-version", "value": "2023-09-01"}], "batchDisabled": false, "transformers": [{"type": "jsonpath", "settings": {"tablePath": "$.value[?(@.properties.schema.tableType == 'CustomLog')]", "columns": [{"path": "$.name", "columnid": "Custom-log table"}, {"path": "$.properties.schema.tableSubType", "columnid": "SubType (Classic vs DCR-based)"}, {"path": "$.properties.schema.tableType", "columnid": "Table type"}, {"path": "$.properties.plan", "columnid": "Plan"}, {"path": "$.properties.retentionInDays", "columnid": "Retention days"}]}}]}
content.title: Classic vs DCR-based custom tables (authoritative - from ARM)

content.json: > If the panel above is empty or errors: set the **Audit workspace** picker just above it and ensure you have **Reader** on that workspace. If your environment's JSONPath doesn't support the `CustomLog` filter, remove the `[?(...)]` filter so it returns all tables and sort/search by *Table type* = `CustomLog`. The two panels below come from `Usage` (KQL) and add volume + recency context per `_CL` table.

content.query:
Usage
| where DataType endswith "_CL"
| summarize GB = round(sum(Quantity) / 1024.0, 2), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
  by ['Custom-log table (_CL)'] = DataType
| extend ['Days since data'] = round(datetime_diff('hour', now(), LastSeen) / 24.0, 1)
| project ['Custom-log table (_CL)'], GB, ['Days since data'], LastSeen
| order by GB desc
content.title: Custom-log (_CL) volume & recency (from Usage)

content.query:
Usage
| where DataType endswith "_CL"
| summarize GB = sum(Quantity) / 1024.0 by bin(TimeGenerated, 1d), DataType
| order by TimeGenerated asc
content.title: Custom-log (_CL) ingestion GB/day

content.json:
### Agent modernisation (secondary)
MMA/OMS retired 31 Aug 2024 and its cloud upload can stop after 2 Mar 2026 - lower priority now, but any remaining **Legacy / MMA** agents below should move to **AMA**. Empty here is normal for a workspace with no VM/agent heartbeats.

content.query:
Heartbeat
| summarize Computers = dcount(Computer), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
  by Category, OSType, Version
| extend Agent = iff(Category has "Azure Monitor Agent", "AMA (modern)", "Legacy / MMA (review)")
| project Agent, Category, OSType, Version, Computers, LastSeen
| order by Computers desc

content.json:
## Engineering Velocity & Change Audit
Detection-as-code throughput and change governance from `SentinelAudit` (`Analytic Rule` operations). Track how many rules are created/updated over time, who is changing detections, and the mix of operations. Useful for sprint reporting and for spotting unexpected or out-of-process changes.

> **This tab needs Sentinel *audit* diagnostics.** If panels are empty, enable Microsoft Sentinel **Settings > Auditing and health monitoring** (streams `SentinelAudit`). For Defender custom-detection change tracking, manage rules as code and review pipeline history.

SentinelAudit
| where SentinelResourceType =~ "Analytic Rule"
| summarize Changes = count() by bin(TimeGenerated, 1d)
| order by TimeGenerated asc

| where SentinelResourceType =~ "Analytic Rule"
| summarize Changes = count() by OperationName

| extend By = tostring(coalesce(tostring(ExtendedProperties.CallerName), tostring(ExtendedProperties.Caller), "Unknown"))

content.json:
## About this workbook

**Detection Engineering Dashboard** gives a detection-engineering team a single pane over the health, coverage, fidelity, efficiency and lifecycle of the analytics-rule portfolio.

### Where to run it
- **Microsoft Defender portal - required**: *Microsoft Sentinel > Threat management > Workbooks*. The **Defender & Custom Detections** tab queries `AlertInfo`, which exists only in the Defender advanced-hunting data plane, so that tab returns nothing anywhere else.
- The Azure portal Sentinel Workbooks gallery is **not supported** for this workbook: you get an incomplete view, and Microsoft Sentinel in the Azure portal retires on **31 March 2027** regardless.

### Data sources (tables)
| Table | Used for |
|---|---|
| `SecurityAlert` | Detection output, MITRE tactic/technique coverage, noise |
| `SecurityIncident` | Fidelity (classification), MTTA/MTTR, aging, ownership |
| `AlertInfo` | **Defender-native** alerts incl. **custom detections** (DetectionSource), service source, techniques |
| `SentinelHealth` | Rule execution health, silent/failing rules (via `ExtendedProperties`) |
| `SentinelAudit` | Detection-as-code velocity and change audit |
| `Usage` | Ingestion volume, cost drivers, stale log sources |

All of these are queryable through the **unified Advanced Hunting** data plane in the Defender portal, so every query here is Advanced-Hunting-native.

> **Portal note:** the **Defender & Custom Detections** tab queries `AlertInfo`, which lives in the Defender advanced-hunting data plane - run the workbook in the **Defender portal**. The **Rule Inventory & Health** and **Engineering Velocity** tabs need Sentinel **Auditing and health monitoring** enabled (they populate `SentinelHealth` / `SentinelAudit`); until then those tabs are intentionally empty while the Defender tab still shows live detection signal.

### Using the new Advanced Hunting / Sentinel data lake data source
Workbooks now support selecting **Sentinel data lake** as a per-step data source, letting you query advanced-hunting and lake tables directly with KQL and **longer retention** (relative time ranges up to 90 days; absolute ranges follow your retention policy).

To switch any high-volume step to the data lake in the Defender portal:
1. Edit the workbook, then edit the query step.
2. Select **Add > Add data source and visualization** (or the step's data-source dropdown).
3. Choose **Sentinel data lake** and pick the workspace.
4. Paste the same KQL and **Run query**. Note: *Set by query* visualization is not supported on the data-lake source, and results should be time-filtered and column-projected for performance.

This template ships every step on the standard **Logs (Analytics)** source so it imports cleanly; flip individual coverage/hunting steps to the data lake in-portal when you want long-retention trend analysis.

### Multi-workspace
- **Workspaces** (multi-select) at the top scopes every log/KQL panel. Select one or many Log Analytics / Microsoft Sentinel workspaces and each query fans out across all of them and unions the results (via `crossComponentResources`). Defaults to **all** workspaces you can access - narrow it for large estates or to focus on one workspace.
- The Lifecycle tab's **Classic vs DCR-based** panel is an ARM call that can target only a *single* workspace at a time, so that tab has a local **Audit workspace** picker (it appears on the Lifecycle tab, not the global bar). It defaults to your first workspace - switch it to audit each workspace's custom tables in turn.

### Interactivity
- **Time range**, **Workspaces**, and **Severity** (multi-select) parameters at the top cross-filter every applicable panel (Overview, Coverage, Defender, Efficacy, Incidents).
- On **Rule Inventory & Health**, click a rule row in *Per-rule execution health* to drill into that rule's run history in the panel below. Clear the selection to see all rules again.
- All grids are sortable (click a column header) and support column search.

### Notes & assumptions
- Health/audit tabs require **Sentinel health & audit** diagnostic logging to be enabled (`SentinelHealth`, `SentinelAudit`). If a panel is empty, enable those diagnostic settings.
- **Lifecycle tab**: the deprecation timeline is a live countdown. The **Classic vs DCR-based** panel reads table metadata (`schema.tableSubType`) from the Log Analytics **Tables API via Azure Resource Manager** - it needs the **Audit workspace (Lifecycle tab)** picker set (auto-populated from your selection) and **Reader** on that workspace; the `_CL` volume panels come from `Usage` (KQL); the agent grid needs `Heartbeat` data.
- MTTA/MTTR are approximations from incident timestamps, not SLA-grade timers.
- Coverage reflects **firing** detections; combine with the portal **MITRE ATT&CK** page for *designed* coverage (rules that exist but haven't fired in-range).
- All queries honour the global **Time range**, **Workspaces**, and **Severity** parameters at the top.

### How to import
1. Defender/Azure portal > Sentinel > **Workbooks > Add workbook > Edit**.
2. Open the **Advanced Editor** (`</>`), replace contents with this JSON, **Apply**, then **Save**.
